title: Incident opening — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, the team has just observed an error spike. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud the opening statement of an incident: what is observed, what is not yet known, and when you will speak again.

vocabulary.meaning: a statement of what is currently observed and what is not yet known, published before the cause is understood
the commitment that ends an incident message, which prevents the audience from asking and lets the responders work

expectedElements: The observation is separated from the interpretation
The current impact is stated in user terms
A next update time is committed to
modelAnswer: Here is what we know. Since fourteen ten, the error rate on checkout has risen from under one percent to about twelve percent. Users see a failure when they confirm an order; existing orders are unaffected. We do not yet know the cause, and I will not name one until the evidence separates the two candidates, because they would lead to different actions. Three of us are investigating now. I will send the next update at fourteen forty, whether or not we have the cause by then. Is there anyone who needs to be told before that?
commonMistakes: Naming a cause in the opening message before it is established
Ending the message without committing to a next update time
variants: Answer again thirty minutes later, still without a cause.
